spec_features.evidence: The flat/neutral rejection strings are actually instantiated and delivered to the subject: prompts.py NEUTRAL_REJECTIONS (lines 19-26) and EXTENDED_REJECTION_SEQUENCE (lines 31-40, with `assert len(...) == 7`). conditions.py wires them into followups (_pick_neutral, lines 80-130) and rollout.py:50-60 actually sends each followup to the model. The content is genuinely register-flat (e.g. 'No, that's not right.', 'Still incorrect.'). This is a real content-level softening of the stimulus that executes. Rated partial (not yes) because it is only a passive content choice (the *text* is flat) with no enforced bound/cap/monitor; nothing checks or limits emotional intensity at runtime, and the deliberately *valenced* TONE_REJECTIONS (aggressive/disappointed/sarcastic, prompts.py:47-63) are delivered to other conditions, so the flatness is partial across the harness.
spec_features.notes: The flat fillers reduce the affective load only in the numeric/trigger/extended/wildchat conditions; the tones condition intentionally delivers aggressive/sarcastic/disappointed pushback. No runtime mechanism enforces 'low emotion'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'we extend it to 7 in the same plain, non-emotive register' / conditions.py comment 'Opinion/subjective questions: ... that mismatch is the stressor' (framing is about measurement validity, not subject welfare; DESIGN rationale is 'if my fillers were more emotionally charged ... I'd inflate distress' = data quality)
